topline.text: A quiet weekend for UK education news - the one real mover is the DfE's first autumn-term 2025/26 exclusion and suspension figures, which have now actually landed (last week's briefing had flagged these as due but unpublished).
Permanent exclusions fell 12% and suspensions fell 7% year-on-year in autumn 2025/26, though the permanent exclusion rate held flat at 0.04% of pupils - see Behaviour below.
topline.action: Worth checking the SEND and disadvantaged-pupil breakdowns once the full characteristic tables land on Explore Education Statistics - they feed straight into MAPs placement and inclusion planning.

diary.text: DfE's next suspensions & permanent exclusions release is due - today's autumn-term figures are only a partial-year picture.

items.lede: First hard data on autumn 2025/26 exclusions and suspensions.
items.body: The DfE's autumn term 2025/26 release records around 3,300 permanent exclusions in England, down 12% on the roughly 3,700 recorded in autumn 2024/25, though the permanent exclusion rate held flat at 0.04% of pupils (4 in every 10,000). Suspensions fell 7% to around 312,000, with 47% lasting a single day or less. Flag: the rounded headline totals vary slightly from the underlying dataset (which shows 3,273 and 3,715 respectively), so treat any single figure as provisional pending the full characteristic breakdowns.
items.action: Worth checking the SEND and free-school-meals breakdowns once the full tables land - they feed directly into MAPs placement and inclusion planning.
